title: Hydraulic requirements for two-motion machine station
scope_statement: Validated scope: generic hydraulic component classes, functional valve behavior, and direct port-to-port connectivity only. Pump/cylinder/reservoir sizing, pressure and flow ratings, line selection, filtration, cooling, prime mover selection, simulation and fabrication approval are explicitly deferred to the later sizing and engineering phases.
design_narrative: Repaired single-station open-circuit hydraulic topology using a fixed-displacement pump, global relief protection, one tandem-center 4/3 StationDCV, two double-acting cylinders, pressure reducing valves on both clamp pressure feeds, a pilot-operated clamp cap holding valve, hydraulic sequence valves for clamp-before-work and work-retract-before-clamp-release ordering, and a mechanically position-operated work-rod supply isolator. Pump pressure branches directly to ReliefValve.P and StationDCV.P. In extend, StationDCV.A feeds ClampExtendReducer and ForwardWorkSequence in parallel; clamp extension occurs first, then ForwardWorkSequence opens for work advance. In retract, StationDCV.B feeds the work-rod supply only through WorkRetractPositionIsolator while also feeding ReverseClampReleaseSequence. At full work retraction the position isolator closes, removing the powered work-retract path; reverse-line pressure can then open ReverseClampReleaseSequence to feed ClampRetractReducer and release/retract the clamp. WorkRodAdvanceReturnCheck provides a one-way rod exhaust path during work advance without allowing reverse supply to bypass the position isolator. All speed behavior remains sizing_only with no metering valves.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: Open-circuit power and 70 bar relief protection
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: Tank.S feeds Pump.S. Pump.P branches directly to ReliefValve.P and StationDCV.P without a manifold component. ReliefValve.T and StationDCV.T return directly to Tank.R. ReliefValve setting/validation enforces the overall system pressure limit not to exceed 70 bar.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: Clamp branch 40 bar pressure reduction with positive clamp hold
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: StationDCV.A feeds ClampExtendReducer.P for reduced-pressure clamp extension; ClampExtendReducer.A feeds ClampPilotCheck.V and ClampPilotCheck.C feeds ClampCylinder.Cap. StationDCV.B can release/retract the clamp only through ReverseClampReleaseSequence and ClampRetractReducer, so the clamp rod feed is also reduced at or below 40 bar. ClampRetractReducer.A also pilots ClampPilotCheck.X to release trapped cap oil. ClampRodReturnCheck provides a one-way rod exhaust path during clamp extension while blocking reverse supply from bypassing the sequence/reducer path.

The forward station command supplies StationDCV.A to both ClampExtendReducer.P and ForwardWorkSequence.P. ForwardWorkSequence remains closed until forward-line pressure rises after clamp force is established, then opens to feed WorkCylinder.Cap. WorkCylinder.Rod returns to StationDCV.B/T through WorkRodAdvanceReturnCheck and, when the position valve is reset open, through WorkRetractPositionIsolator. Working stroke time and force remain pump/cylinder sizing items; no flow-control valve is added.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: Position-isolated work retraction with explicit cap return
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: In StationDCV retract state, StationDCV.B supplies WorkCylinder.Rod only through WorkRetractPositionIsolator while WorkCylinder.Cap exhausts through WorkCapReturnCheck.P-A to StationDCV.A and then through StationDCV.A-T to Tank.R. At full retraction, WorkRetractPositionIsolator closes and blocks further powered rod supply.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: Hydraulic work-retract-before-clamp-release sequence with work-path isolation
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: StationDCV.B retracts the work cylinder through the open WorkRetractPositionIsolator while ReverseClampReleaseSequence remains closed. At full work retract, WorkRetractPositionIsolator closes so the working actuator no longer has a complete powered motion path. Reverse-line pressure can then open ReverseClampReleaseSequence to feed ClampRetractReducer.P. ClampRetractReducer.A supplies ClampCylinder.Rod and ClampPilotCheck.X, enabling clamp release after work return without an electrical pressure switch.

The selected motion decisions specify sizing_only speed realization, so working-axis stroke time and force are realized by pump flow and cylinder effective-area sizing rather than added flow-control valves.

design_decisions.decision: Use one tandem-center station DCV for both cylinders instead of split-axis DCVs.
design_decisions.rationale: A single extend command pressurizes the common forward line so clamp extension and the sequenced work-advance branch are part of one hydraulic command. Tandem center unloads the fixed pump in neutral while blocking work ports.

design_decisions.decision: Use hydraulic sequence valves for both forward and reverse ordering.
design_decisions.rationale: ForwardWorkSequence gates work advance until clamp pressure rises. ReverseClampReleaseSequence gates clamp release until the work-retract end-position isolation has removed the active work path and reverse-line pressure rises. This implements hydraulic ordering without an electrical pressure switch.

design_decisions.decision: Add a position-operated isolation valve in the work-rod retract supply path.
design_decisions.rationale: WorkRetractPositionIsolator is open during work retract and closed at the fully retracted trip. Its closed state blocks StationDCV.B supply to WorkCylinder.Rod during clamp release, repairing the forbidden active working path.

design_decisions.decision: Add a work-rod exhaust check independent of the position isolator.
design_decisions.rationale: WorkRodAdvanceReturnCheck provides declared WorkCylinder.Rod exhaust to StationDCV.B/T during work advance even if the position isolator is closed at the retracted start position, while its reverse blocking prevents StationDCV.B from bypassing the isolator during retract/release.

design_decisions.decision: Limit both clamp extension and clamp release/retract feeds with pressure reducing valves.
design_decisions.rationale: The clamp function must remain at or below 40 bar while the main relief may be set up to 70 bar. ClampExtendReducer limits the clamp cap feed and ClampRetractReducer prevents reverse clamp release/retract pressure from bypassing the clamp pressure limit.

design_decisions.decision: Hold clamp force with a pilot-operated check at the clamp cap end.
design_decisions.rationale: ClampPilotCheck allows free flow from the reduced clamp cap feed into the clamp cylinder, blocks cap-end reverse flow during working advance and return, and opens only when the reduced clamp retract line pilots X.

design_decisions.decision: Use a fixed-displacement open-circuit power unit with direct relief protection.
design_decisions.rationale: The open circuit uses Tank, Pump, and ReliefValve in the minimum power path. The relief valve protects the pump pressure line and returns excess flow to Tank.R.

design_decisions.decision: Do not add flow-control valves for the working stroke time or clamp speed.
design_decisions.rationale: All motion-control decisions specify sizing_only speed realization. Pump flow and cylinder effective areas will be sized to meet the approximate working travel/time target and clamp performance without deliberate throttling.

assumptions: Sequence valve thresholds, pressure-reducer settings, relief setting, cylinder bore/rod dimensions, pump flow, pressure losses and acceptance tolerances are deferred to sizing and commissioning.
Repeated component ports represent direct branched hydraulic lines; no tee, manifold, hose, or line component is inserted.
The working branch up-to-60 bar condition can be satisfied by actuator sizing/process load unless the specifier later requires an explicit working-branch pressure reducer.
WorkRetractPositionIsolator is mechanically arranged so it is open before the full-retract trip, remains open through the work-retract stroke, and closes at the confirmed fully retracted condition.
open_issues: Sizing must establish relief setting, reducing-valve settings, sequence thresholds, cylinder areas, pump flow, pressure losses, and acceptance tolerances.
Confirm whether the working branch 'up to 60 bar' statement is a sizing limit only or requires an explicit working-branch pressure reducer.
Position trip/reset arrangement for WorkRetractPositionIsolator must be validated so it is open through the work-retract stroke and closed at the fully retracted condition.
A position-operated valve is selected without a position-triggered phase requirement.

The topology makes the reverse-order interlock depend on WorkRetractPositionIsolator, a mechanically position-operated bypass/isolator, even though the brief and supported research call for hydraulic pressure/sequence logic and do not specify a position-triggered phase device. Its asserted state changes are essential: open for work retract, closed at full retract to remove the powered work-rod path and force ReverseClampReleaseSequence to open. That is an unsupported added control element rather than a justified hydraulic sequence/check topology, so the clamp-release-after-work-retract function relies on unjustified functional complexity.

research_coverage.summary: Most actuator, sequencing, holding, and branch-pressure-reduction needs are supported by cited engineering sources. However, the overall open-circuit power topology is still incomplete because the accumulated evidence explicitly lacks a cited source for the reservoir-to-pump suction/inlet connection. Since the system_power_and_relief need is critical and includes suction, pump, relief, return, and reservoir topology, design should not proceed until that missing suction-flow-path claim is supported.

items.rationale: Relief-valve placement, relief discharge to tank/reservoir, fixed-displacement pump overpressure protection, relief setting as maximum system pressure, and return/drain-to-reservoir paths are well supported by cited textbook/technical sources in T1. But T1 explicitly states that evidence for the tank-to-pump suction line was not found. Because the need requires complete suction, pump, pressure-relief, return, and reservoir topology, this critical need remains partial.

T2 supports the component class and connection pattern for a double-acting clamp cylinder controlled by a 4-way directional control valve, including A-to-cap/B-to-rod hookup, extend/retract actuation, and neutral spool behavior options. Load-holding neutral safety for the clamp is further addressed by the separate pilot-operated check valve evidence in T3.

T2 supports sizing-only speed behavior using pump flow and cylinder effective area rather than additional speed-control topology. T3 supports the hold phase using pilot-operated check/load-lock logic, and T5 supports pressure-sequence transition from clamp extension/clamping to the working actuator phase and later clamp release after the work return sequence.

T3 provides cited support for pilot-operated check valves placed at or near actuator work ports: free flow into the actuator, reverse-flow blocking from the load, pilot pressure release, and cross-piloting from the opposite work line for a double-acting cylinder. It also provides safety rationale that directional valve neutral/leakage alone should not be relied on as the holding element.
T2 supports a double-acting working cylinder operated by a 4-way directional control valve, including A-to-cap/B-to-rod hookup, extend/retract function, and neutral spool behavior options.

T2 supports sizing-only advance/retract speed based on flow rate and cylinder effective area, including the distinction between cap-end area for extension and annular rod-end area for retraction. T5 supports the ordered working-actuator phase placement within the multi-actuator sequence.

T5 provides cited support for a hydraulic pressure-sequence topology: clamp actuator receives flow first, a normally closed sequence valve blocks the working branch until clamp pressure rises, bypass checks preserve reverse flow, and sequence-valve drains are used where both work ports may be pressurized. It also cites a two-cylinder sequence order of clamp/cylinder 1 extend, work/cylinder 2 extend, work/cylinder 2 retract, and clamp/cylinder 1 retract, with clamp pressure maintained during the work stroke/return by a pilot-operated check valve.

T4 provides cited support for using a pressure-reducing valve in only the lower-pressure clamp branch, controlling downstream pressure to the clamp circuit while the main system relief remains at the higher system pressure. It also supports placement in the branch/outlet side feeding the clamp circuit, use of a reducing/relieving style where trapped downstream pressure must be relieved, and the requirement for an open drain/third port to tank.

missing_or_weak_information: Critical missing claim: the reservoir/tank must supply the pump inlet through a suction line in an open hydraulic circuit, completing the path reservoir → pump inlet/suction → pump outlet/pressure circuit → valves/actuators/relief → return/tank.

Noncritical limitation: some sources for neutral spool examples are commercial product pages rather than primary standards, but the essential DCV connection and center-condition principles are supported by technical sources.

Noncritical limitation: return-order sequencing evidence includes some examples that mention solenoids/limit switches; however, the cited sequence-valve principles and two-cylinder sequence circuit still support the hydraulic topology pattern.
